title: Forge 8: mini-batches, early stopping and the training loop

wrong.batches_not_shuffled.py: minibatches returns the indices in order (no shuffle)
wrong.batches_same_order_every_epoch.py: the epoch is ignored when seeding, so every epoch sees the same order
wrong.batches_seed_ignored.py: the seed is ignored: a fresh unseeded generator is used
wrong.batches_drop_last.py: the ragged last batch is silently dropped
wrong.batches_with_replacement.py: indices are sampled with replacement, so some examples repeat and others are missed
wrong.es_patience_off_by_one.py: training stops one epoch late (bad_epochs > patience)
wrong.es_counter_never_resets.py: an improvement does not reset the bad-epoch counter, so stops come too early
wrong.es_ties_count_as_improvement.py: a tie counts as an improvement (<=), so a flat loss never stops
wrong.es_min_delta_ignored.py: min_delta is ignored: any decrease counts as progress
wrong.es_snapshot_is_a_view.py: best_params holds references to the live arrays, so later training overwrites the 'best' weights
wrong.es_restore_rebinds.py: restore assigns to the loop variable instead of writing into the live arrays, so the model is unchanged
wrong.es_best_epoch_off_by_one.py: best_epoch is off by one (epochs counted from 1)
wrong.fit_never_restores.py: fit returns the weights of the last epoch it ran instead of restoring the best
wrong.fit_ignores_max_epochs.py: fit keeps going until early stopping triggers, ignoring max_epochs
wrong.fit_validates_on_train.py: the 'validation' loss is computed on the training set
wrong.fit_unweighted_train_loss.py: the epoch train loss is the plain mean of batch losses (the short last batch counts too much)
wrong.fit_steps_on_validation.py: the validation pass is followed by an optimiser step, so the model trains on validation data
wrong.fit_epoch_not_passed.py: fit passes epoch 0 to minibatches every time, so every epoch shuffles identically

hints: minibatches: order = np.random.default_rng([seed, epoch]).permutation(n), then slice [i:i+batch_size] for i in range(0, n, batch_size).
EarlyStopping.update: improved = val_loss < best_loss - min_delta. If improved, store best_loss, best_epoch and [p.copy() for p in params]; reset the counter. Otherwise increment it.
restore must write INTO the live arrays: p[...] = best. Assigning a new list would not change the model.
fit: for each epoch accumulate loss * len(idx) over batches and divide by len(Xtr). Compute the validation loss with the same loss_and_backward call (ignore its gradients).
Test your fit by checking that after it returns, the model's validation loss equals min(val_losses).
